title: Ground equations: finite congruence closure and models
summary: Decide finite equations and disequations by identifying retained subterms, and construct a finite structure whenever the test succeeds.
abstract: If two names denote the same object, applying the same function to them must give the same result. But equal function values do not force equal inputs. These simple rules are enough to decide whether a finite collection of equations and disequations between terms without variables can hold in some structure. We keep only the subterms occurring in the input and repeatedly add the equalities they force. When no requested inequality is contradicted, the resulting classes of terms, together with one extra element, form an explicit finite model. The construction explains both why the test terminates and how functions can be interpreted even on inputs that never appeared in the problem.
